report.executive_summary: All four charger packages qualify under the client gates, so lowest measured energy decides. P2 leads at 15 kWh per common charging acceptance test, ahead of P3 (24), P1 (44) and P4 (64) — gaps of 9, 29 and 49 kWh. P2 also carries the fewest defects (1) and second-best quality (95). This brief re-derives the gates, ranking and gaps from the trusted table alone, tests the outcome under tightened gates, and separates measured facts from open questions. The recommendation is P2.
report.figure_caption: Decision diagram: proportional 0–70 kWh energy bars on a stated 8 px-per-kWh axis, P2 leading, beside the gate-screening workflow from trusted table to verified P2 recommendation.

recommendation.rationale: All four packages qualify, so lowest energy decides. P2's 15 kWh leads P3 by 9, P1 by 29 and P4 by 49, with the fewest defects (1) and second-best quality (95). It strictly dominates P3 and P4 on every recorded field and remains the winner under every tightened gate that admits it. No open question can plausibly close a 9 kWh gap.

sections.body: The quality gate requires at least 80. All four packages clear it: P1 at 100, P2 at 95, P3 at 91 and P4 at 88, so the gate removes nothing. The defect gate allows at most 5 raw counts: P1 and P3 sit at 3, P2 at 1, and P4 exactly at 5 — compliant with zero margin. Because every candidate qualifies, the lowest-ID tie-break never activates and the decision rests entirely on energy. The margins differ sharply: P4's zero defect margin is the table's only boundary case, which matters if a single additional defect appears in any future re-test.
sections.heading: Gate Screening from the Trusted Table

sections.body: All energy figures share one output, load and acceptance-test basis, so they compare directly. Ascending order: P2 15, P3 24, P1 44, P4 64 kWh input per common charging acceptance test. Leader gaps: 9 kWh to P3, 29 to P1 and 49 to P4; P4 consumes roughly 4.3 times P2's energy for the identical specified charging output. No energy tie exists, so no tie-break is needed. The 9 kWh P2-over-P3 margin is the smallest gap, yet P2 also holds the best defect count and better quality, so no recorded field favors P3 over P2.
sections.heading: Energy Ranking and Leader Gaps

sections.body: The client-correct answer survives every tightening that keeps P2 eligible. A quality gate of 95 leaves P1 and P2, and P2 still has the lowest energy; at 96 only P1 remains and wins by default. A defect limit of 4 leaves P1, P2 and P3, with P2 still leading; at 2 only P2 survives. Strict dominance reinforces this: P2 beats P3 on quality (95 vs 91), defects (1 vs 3) and energy (15 vs 24), and beats P4 on all three recorded fields (95 vs 88, 1 vs 5, 15 vs 64).
sections.heading: Robustness Under Tightened Gates

sections.body: Measured facts: the trusted table's three columns on the common basis, the verified ranking and the stated gaps. Open questions: single readings only, so repeat-run variance behind the 15 and 24 kWh figures is unknown; defect severity is absent; cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified and excluded from ranking. Under the supplied policy the qualifying set is all four candidates and lowest energy selects P2. The analyst's separately locked ballot is recorded independently of this brief; any divergence is carried to the next handover as an open item, as in prior rounds.
